assessment.title: Electrical Knowledge Assessment
assessment.description: A knowledge assessment of electrical safety, theory, circuits, installation, and diagnostics. Scores are not a license or certification.

version.instructions: Answer each question to the best of your knowledge. You can go back and change answers before submitting. This is a knowledge assessment, not a license or certification.

categories.name: Safety, Tools & Work Practices
categories.description: Electrical safety, tools, and professional work practices.

questions.prompt: Before touching conductors in a panel, what is the safest sequence?
questions.explanation: Identify the circuit, de-energize, lock out/tag out, and verify absence of voltage with a meter that has been tested on a known live source.

choices.body: De-energize, lock out/tag out, and verify with a meter
Grab the conductor quickly to see if it shocks
Rely only on a breaker handle position without testing
Remove the equipment grounding conductor first so the circuit cannot return

questions.prompt: Why is eye protection required when cutting, drilling, or pulling wire in occupied walls?
questions.explanation: Metal shavings, masonry dust, and snapping conductors can injure eyes. Safety glasses are basic PPE.

choices.body: Debris and snapping conductors can injure the eyes
Eye protection is only for welding
Electrical work cannot produce flying particles
A paper dust mask is complete eye protection

questions.prompt: A GFCI device is intended primarily to protect against:
questions.explanation: A GFCI opens when it detects imbalance between the ungrounded and grounded conductors, reducing shock hazard. It is not an overcurrent device for conductor ampacity.

choices.body: Shock from ground-fault current through a person or leakage path
Overloaded conductors the same way a breaker does
High utility voltage sags
Low transformer impedance

questions.prompt: Why should jewelry and conductive watches be removed around energized equipment?
questions.explanation: Metal jewelry can bridge live parts and cause burns. De-energize when possible; do not wear conductive jewelry around live work.

choices.body: Metal jewelry can short live parts and cause burns
Jewelry improves grip on insulated tools
Conductive jewelry is required PPE
Watches protect against arc flash

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an insulated hand tool rated for electrical work?
questions.explanation: The insulation is a barrier if contact with an energized part occurs. It is not a substitute for de-energizing, and damaged insulation must not be used.

choices.body: To provide a dielectric barrier if a live part is contacted
To magnetize fasteners
To increase torque beyond the tool’s mechanical rating
To replace lockout/tagout

questions.prompt: A ladder used near overhead electrical lines should be:
questions.explanation: Use nonconductive ladders and maintain safe approach distances. Metal ladders near overhead lines are a shock hazard.

choices.body: Nonconductive and kept a safe distance from overhead lines
Aluminum, because metal is safer near power lines
Placed so the rails rest on the conductors for stability
Wet, so it cannot conduct

questions.prompt: Why must a circuit be identified before it is opened for repair?
questions.explanation: The wrong breaker can leave the circuit live. Trace, identify, de-energize, and verify. Guessing among similar breakers is unsafe.

choices.body: So the correct circuit is de-energized and verified dead
Identification is only for billing the utility
Any breaker in the panel de-energizes every circuit
Neutral bars cannot remain energized if one breaker is off

questions.prompt: What is lockout/tagout intended to prevent?
questions.explanation: LOTO prevents unexpected re-energization while someone is working. A note on a phone is not a lockout.

choices.body: Unexpected energization or startup while work is in progress
Utility brownouts
GFCI nuisance trips only
Voltage drop in long feeders

questions.prompt: An arc-flash hazard exists when:
questions.explanation: A fault can release intense heat and light. De-energize when possible and use appropriate PPE and procedures when live work is justified. Cotton street clothes are not arc-rated PPE.

choices.body: A fault can release a high-energy electrical explosion of heat and light
Only when working on fiber-optic cable
Only on extra-low-voltage doorbells
Never on 208/240-volt equipment

questions.prompt: Why should a meter be checked on a known live source before and after proving a circuit dead?
questions.explanation: A failed meter can read zero on a live circuit. Live-dead-live verification confirms the instrument works.

choices.body: To confirm the meter is working so a zero reading is trustworthy
Because meters cannot be trusted on known live sources
To drain the meter’s internal battery faster
To magnetize the probes

questions.prompt: A confined space with electrical equipment may also have atmospheric hazards. What should be considered before extended work?
questions.explanation: Vaults and pits can have oxygen deficiency or toxic gases in addition to shock hazards. Assess the atmosphere and electrical isolation together.

choices.body: Atmospheric hazards as well as electrical hazards
Only noise, never atmosphere
That vaults are always safe if a flashlight works
That a paper mask is complete confined-space protection

questions.prompt: Damaged insulation on a flexible cord should be:
questions.explanation: Damaged cords are a shock and fire hazard. Take them out of service. Tape is not a permanent repair for portable cord on a construction site.

choices.body: Taken out of service and replaced or properly repaired
Wrapped with a single layer of masking tape as a permanent repair
Used only in wet locations so the water cools the copper
Overfused so the cord can carry more current

questions.prompt: When drilling into a wall, why is looking for existing cables, pipes, and a safe boring location important?
questions.explanation: Drilling into concealed conductors can cause shock and arc. Use detectors, open a visual inspection where needed, and follow boring/notching rules.

choices.body: Concealed conductors can be punctured, creating shock and arc hazards
Cables are never run in walls
Drill bits cannot cut copper
A metal fish tape in a live conduit is the preferred locator

questions.prompt: Why is standing on a wet floor while working in a panel a concern even if the panel cover is on?
questions.explanation: Moisture lowers contact resistance to ground and increases shock severity. Dry, stable footing and de-energized work reduce risk.

choices.body: Water lowers resistance to ground and increases shock risk
Water is an insulator at panel voltages
Wet floors reduce arc-flash energy
GFCI on a lighting circuit makes wet-floor panel work risk-free

questions.prompt: Temporary jobsite lighting and cords should be arranged so that:
questions.explanation: Cords should be protected from damage, not create trip hazards, and be suitable for the location. Daisy-chaining damaged strips is a common fire/trip hazard.

choices.body: They are protected from damage and do not create trip or shock hazards
They run through doorways un-protected so they are visible
They are covered with carpet in a wet walkway
They are fused above the cord’s ampacity so they do not trip

questions.prompt: A live-front panelboard with the cover off should be treated as:
questions.explanation: Exposed energized parts require work practices and PPE appropriate to the hazard, and work should be de-energized when possible. Casual clothing is not adequate.

choices.body: An exposed-energized-parts hazard until it is de-energized and verified
Safe because the breakers have handles
Safe if the worker is wearing a cotton hoodie
Safe for jewelry because the bus is recessed

questions.prompt: Why must unused openings in boxes and enclosures be closed?
questions.explanation: Openings expose live parts, allow debris entry, and can violate listing. Use listed closures, not cardboard.

choices.body: To prevent exposure of live parts and keep the enclosure’s protection intact
To increase ventilation around breakers as a design goal
Because openings improve GFCI function
So rodents can inspect splices

questions.prompt: A helper is about to reset a breaker that tripped while someone is still working downstream. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Never re-energize a circuit until it is confirmed clear and people are clear. Investigate the trip. Communication is part of LOTO.

choices.body: Do not re-energize until the circuit is clear and the cause is understood
Reset immediately so work can continue under load
Tape the breaker on so it cannot trip again
Install a larger breaker without investigation

questions.prompt: Voltage-rated gloves must be:
questions.explanation: Inspected, used within rating and date requirements, and paired with leather protectors as required. Damaged gloves must be removed from service.

choices.body: Inspected and used within their rating; damaged gloves taken out of service
Used after cutting off the leather protectors for better feel as a standard practice
Held together with tape after a puncture
Used as the only control while standing in water on an unidentified circuit

questions.prompt: A 480-volt motor disconnect is tagged out, but a separate control-power transformer still energizes a 120-volt circuit in the same enclosure. What is the lesson?
questions.explanation: Equipment can have multiple energy sources. Isolating the motor feeder does not isolate control power, heaters, or foreign voltage. Identify all sources and verify each.

choices.body: All energy sources in the enclosure must be identified, isolated, and verified
Motor disconnects always isolate every voltage in the cabinet
120-volt control circuits cannot shock
Tags without energy isolation are sufficient if they say DANGER

questions.prompt: An electrician must work near an overhead line that cannot be de-energized. What is the appropriate approach?
questions.explanation: Maintain required approach distances, use spotters, nonconductive equipment, and utility coordination. Do not guess distances from the ground with a metal tape.

choices.body: Maintain required clearances, use nonconductive equipment, and coordinate with the utility
Touch the line with a metal fish tape to see if it is live
Assume insulated service drop covering is touch-safe for a ladder
Raise a metal scaffold until it is just below the conductors

questions.prompt: A fault occurs and a worker is frozen to a live part. What is the correct first priority for a rescuer?
questions.explanation: Do not grab the person with bare hands. De-energize or use an insulating rescue method. Then call emergency services. This is about not becoming a second victim.

choices.body: De-energize or separate the person with insulating means; do not touch them with bare hands
Pull the person free with bare hands as fast as possible
Pour water on both people to cool the burn while they remain in contact
Reset the breaker so the circuit can help let go

questions.prompt: Infrared scanning of a loaded panel is planned. Why is removing the dead-front without a work plan a problem?
questions.explanation: Removing covers exposes live parts. Scanning should follow electrical safety procedures, appropriate PPE, and closed-cover IR windows when used. Do not casually open a loaded 480-volt board in street clothes.

choices.body: Removing covers exposes live parts and requires an electrical-safety work plan
IR scans are harmless because cameras are plastic
Loaded panels cannot arc if the camera is battery powered
Street clothes are arc-rated if they are dark-colored

questions.prompt: A generator is backfeeding a building during an outage through a dryer receptacle. Why is this unsafe?
questions.explanation: Backfeeding can energize service conductors and kill a lineworker, and it can overpower cords and transfer equipment. Use a listed transfer switch or interlock that prevents utility and generator interconnection.

choices.body: It can energize utility lines and overloads unlisted cords/connections
Portable generators cannot produce lethal voltage
Backfeeding through a receptacle is the listed transfer method
Utility transformers block all backfeed by design in every case

categories.name: Electrical Theory
categories.description: Voltage, current, resistance, power, and magnetic fundamentals.

questions.prompt: Ohm’s law relates voltage, current, and resistance as:
questions.explanation: E = I × R (or V = I R). Power is a different quantity (P = I × E).

choices.body: Voltage equals current times resistance
Voltage equals current divided by resistance always
Current equals voltage times resistance
Resistance equals voltage times current

questions.prompt: Current in a circuit is:
questions.explanation: Current is the flow of electric charge, measured in amperes.

choices.body: The flow of electric charge
Opposition to flow, measured in ohms
Electrical pressure, measured in volts
Energy stored in a capacitor only

questions.prompt: Resistance is measured in:
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms. Conductance is measured in siemens; inductance in henries; capacitance in farads.

choices.body: Ohms
Amperes
Volts
Watts

questions.prompt: In a series circuit, current is:
questions.explanation: Series current is the same through each component. Voltage divides across resistances.

choices.body: The same through each component
Different through each resistor and lowest at the source
Always zero after the first lamp
Inversely proportional to voltage only, never resistance

questions.prompt: In a parallel circuit, voltage across each branch is:
questions.explanation: Parallel branches share the same voltage; currents add.

choices.body: The same across each branch
Split so each branch gets a fraction of the source voltage always
Zero on all but one branch
Equal to the sum of the branch voltages

questions.prompt: Power in a DC circuit can be calculated as:
questions.explanation: P = I × E, also P = I²R and P = E²/R for resistive circuits.

choices.body: Volts times amperes
Volts divided by amperes only
Ohms times volts only
Amperes divided by ohms only

questions.prompt: A transformer’s primary function is to:
questions.explanation: A transformer transfers AC power between circuits, typically changing voltage by the turns ratio. It does not create DC without additional components.

choices.body: Change AC voltage (and current) between circuits by magnetic coupling
Convert AC to chemical energy
Store energy like a battery
Increase frequency from 60 Hz to 400 Hz automatically

questions.prompt: A 120-volt heater draws 10 amperes. What is the power?

choices.body: 1,200 watts
12 watts
1.2 watts
120 kilowatts

questions.prompt: Two 10-ohm resistors in parallel have an equivalent resistance of:
questions.explanation: Equal parallel resistors: R/n = 10/2 = 5 ohms.

choices.body: 5 ohms
20 ohms
10 ohms
100 ohms

questions.prompt: A conductor’s resistance increases when:
questions.explanation: Resistance rises with length, with higher temperature (for copper), and with smaller cross-section. It is not reduced by using a longer wire.

choices.body: It is longer, smaller in cross-section, or hotter (for copper)
It is shorter and thicker
It is cooled and shortened
Its circular mil area is increased while length stays the same

questions.prompt: Inductive loads such as motors cause current to:
questions.explanation: Inductance makes current lag voltage. Power factor is less than 1. This is why motor circuits can have higher current than a same-wattage resistive heater.

choices.body: Lag the voltage
Lead the voltage like a capacitor always does in every motor
Remain exactly in phase regardless of inductance
Stop at the first winding

questions.prompt: A capacitor stores energy in:
questions.explanation: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field between plates. An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.

choices.body: An electric field
A magnetic field only, like an inductor
A chemical reaction like a primary battery as its main mechanism
A rotating magnetic field in the rotor bars

questions.prompt: Kirchhoff’s current law states that:
questions.explanation: The algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero: current in equals current out.

choices.body: The currents entering a node equal the currents leaving it
Voltage is the same on every series component
Power is always conserved as heat only
Resistance is independent of temperature for all metals

questions.prompt: A 3-ohm and a 6-ohm resistor are in series on 18 volts. Current is:
questions.explanation: Rt = 9 ohms; I = 18/9 = 2 A.

choices.body: 2 amperes
6 amperes
9 amperes
0.5 ampere

questions.prompt: RMS voltage for a sine wave is significant because:
questions.explanation: RMS is the effective value that produces the same heating in a resistor as a DC voltage of that value. Meters typically display RMS for AC power circuits.

choices.body: It is the effective value related to heating in a resistive load
It is always 0.5 times peak for a sine wave
It is the same as average voltage for all waveforms
It only applies to batteries

questions.prompt: A motor nameplate lists FLA. This is most nearly:
questions.explanation: Full-load amperes is the current at rated load, voltage, and frequency. LRA is locked-rotor (starting) current, which is much higher.

choices.body: Current at rated load and voltage
Locked-rotor current at start
The branch-circuit breaker rating always
The grounding-electrode conductor size

questions.prompt: Power factor is:
questions.explanation: Power factor is real power divided by apparent power (W/VA). It is 1.0 for a pure resistor and lower for inductive motors.

choices.body: Real power divided by apparent power
Voltage divided by current
Resistance times current squared only
The transformer turns ratio

questions.prompt: In a balanced 208Y/120-volt system, the voltage from line to neutral is:
questions.explanation: Line-to-neutral is 120 volts; line-to-line is 208 volts.

choices.body: 120 volts
208 volts
240 volts
480 volts

questions.prompt: A short circuit differs from an overload because a short circuit is:
questions.explanation: A short is an unintended low-resistance path and very high current. An overload is excess current within the load path, often modestly above rating.

choices.body: An unintended low-resistance path that can produce very high current
A slight increase in load current above FLA only
Always a high-resistance leakage through a person
A transformer with too many secondary turns

questions.prompt: A 240-volt single-phase load draws 20 A at a power factor of 0.80. Approximate real power is:

choices.body: 3,840 watts
4,800 watts
240 watts
16 watts

questions.prompt: A transformer is 480 V primary to 120 V secondary. If primary current is 5 A (ignoring losses), secondary current is about:
questions.explanation: Ampere-turns/power balance: 480×5 ≈ 120×Is → Is ≈ 20 A. Current inverses with voltage.

choices.body: 20 amperes
5 amperes
1.25 amperes
480 amperes

questions.prompt: Skin effect at higher frequency causes AC current to:
questions.explanation: Current crowds toward the conductor surface, raising effective resistance. It is more relevant at higher frequencies than at 60 Hz for typical small building wire, but the principle is still tested in theory.

choices.body: Crowd toward the conductor surface, raising effective resistance
Travel only in the steel conduit, never the copper
Stop entirely above 60 Hz
Become DC automatically

questions.prompt: A three-phase motor runs with one supply phase lost (single-phasing). What is a likely result?
questions.explanation: The motor may try to run with excessive current in the remaining windings, overheating. It should be protected and taken off line; it will not produce full torque.

choices.body: Overheating and reduced torque in the remaining windings
Higher efficiency than on three phases
No current in any winding
Automatic conversion to a generator at higher voltage

questions.prompt: Why can a high-impedance voltmeter show voltage on an open, parallel-run conductor?
questions.explanation: Capacitive coupling can impress a phantom voltage. A low-impedance meter or a small load collapses it. Treat unknown readings carefully; verify with an appropriate method.

choices.body: Capacitive coupling can create a phantom voltage that cannot supply much current
The conductor must be solidly connected to the utility
Phantom voltage only exists on fiber
High-impedance meters cannot display AC

categories.name: Wiring, Circuits & Components
categories.description: Branch circuits, devices, and electrical components.

questions.prompt: A typical branch circuit consists of:
questions.explanation: Ungrounded (hot) conductors, a grounded (neutral) conductor when required, an equipment grounding conductor, and an overcurrent device.

choices.body: Circuit conductors, an overcurrent device, and an equipment grounding path as required
Only a transformer with no overcurrent device
Only a grounding electrode with no ungrounded conductor
A water pipe used as the only circuit conductor

questions.prompt: A switch is generally installed in the:
questions.explanation: Switches interrupt the ungrounded conductor. Switching the grounded (neutral) conductor alone can leave equipment energized.

choices.body: Ungrounded (hot) conductor
Equipment grounding conductor only
Grounding electrode conductor only
Neutral only, leaving the hot continuous as a standard lighting practice

questions.prompt: The equipment grounding conductor is intended to:
questions.explanation: Bond non-current-carrying metal so fault current can return and open the overcurrent device.

choices.body: Provide a low-impedance path for fault current
Carry normal load current in place of the neutral
Increase voltage at the load
Replace the overcurrent device

questions.prompt: A receptacle’s grounding slot (U-shape or green screw) connects to:
questions.explanation: The equipment grounding conductor, which bonds the yoke and downstream metal.

choices.body: The equipment grounding conductor
The ungrounded hot only
A satellite dish mast as the only required path
The utility meter’s potential coil

questions.prompt: Overcurrent devices are selected to protect:
questions.explanation: Conductors and equipment from overload and fault current, within their listings and the circuit design.

choices.body: Conductors and equipment from excessive current
Only the utility transformer primary
The grounding electrode from lightning exclusively
Fiber-optic cables from light overload

questions.prompt: A three-way switch loop is used to:
questions.explanation: Control a lighting load from two locations. It is not a series heater circuit.

choices.body: Control a load from two locations
Increase voltage from 120 to 240
Create a separately derived system
Bond a water pipe

questions.prompt: A fuse or breaker that opens frequently on a circuit may indicate:
questions.explanation: Overload, a fault, or a device mismatch. Replacing it with a larger rating without investigation is unsafe.

choices.body: Overload, a short/ground fault, or an incorrectly sized device
That the circuit needs a larger unlisted fuse as the first action
That the grounding conductor is too large
That GFCI protection should be removed

questions.prompt: A multiwire branch circuit shares a neutral. A key safety practice is:
questions.explanation: The ungrounded conductors should be on different phases/legs so the neutral carries difference current, and a means to simultaneously disconnect them is required in many installations. Disconnecting the neutral under load can overvoltage loads.

choices.body: Keep the ungrounded conductors on different legs and do not open the shared neutral under load
Land both hots on the same bus stab so the neutral carries 2× current as a design
Use the equipment grounding conductor as the shared neutral
Size the shared neutral as a signaling pair

questions.prompt: Voltage drop in a long feeder is a concern because:
questions.explanation: Excessive drop causes motors to run hot, lights to dim, and electronics to misbehave. Increasing conductor size or reducing length/load are typical remedies.

choices.body: Loads may overheat or perform poorly at reduced voltage
Voltage drop increases conductor ampacity
Voltage drop is required to operate GFCIs
Motors always need at least 20% drop to start

questions.prompt: A GFCI receptacle protecting downstream receptacles does so through:
questions.explanation: The load-side terminals feed downstream devices through the GFCI’s current transformer. Line and load reversed will not protect downstream (and may not reset).

choices.body: Its load-side terminals feeding those devices
The equipment grounding conductor only
A wireless signal to the panel
The water piping

questions.prompt: An AFCI is intended to protect against:
questions.explanation: Arc-faults that can ignite nearby materials. It is complementary to, not the same as, GFCI personnel protection.

choices.body: Arcing faults that can start fires
Only utility high voltage
Only motor inrush as a design
Only harmonic currents in LEDs

questions.prompt: A contactor or relay coil is on a control circuit, while its contacts may switch:
questions.explanation: Coils are often lower voltage; contacts can switch line-voltage loads. Treat both as possible shock hazards.

choices.body: A separate, possibly higher-voltage load circuit
Only the same extra-low voltage as the coil in every case
Only fiber-optic signals
Only DC when the coil is AC, always

questions.prompt: Why are white conductors used as hots in switch loops required to be reidentified?
questions.explanation: So the next electrician does not treat an ungrounded conductor as a neutral. Reidentify with marking where required.

choices.body: To show that the conductor is being used as an ungrounded conductor, not a neutral
To increase ampacity
To allow the white wire to be used as a grounding conductor
Reidentification is only for fiber jackets

questions.prompt: A motor starter’s overload relay is intended to protect against:
questions.explanation: Sustained overcurrent in the motor from mechanical overload. Short-circuit/ground-fault protection is a different function, usually fuses or a breaker.

choices.body: Sustained motor overcurrent from overload
Only lightning on the utility line
Only the control transformer primary inrush as its sole job
The grounding electrode resistance

questions.prompt: Dimming an LED lighting load with an incompatible dimmer often causes:
questions.explanation: Flicker, buzzing, overheating, or failure. Match the dimmer to the load type and listing.

choices.body: Flicker, noise, or overheating
An automatic increase in conductor ampacity
Conversion of the branch circuit to three-phase
A listed substitute for AFCI protection

questions.prompt: A transformer supplying a 120/240-volt panel is a separately derived system when:
questions.explanation: When there is no direct electrical connection between primary and secondary (typical isolation transformer) and the secondary is grounded as required. The bonding/grounding arrangement must be made at the derived system.

choices.body: The secondary is not electrically derived through a direct conductive path from the primary and is grounded/bonded as a new system
A receptacle is added on a branch circuit
A GFCI is installed
A three-way switch is added

questions.prompt: Why should aluminum branch-circuit terminations be made with listed connectors and proper torque?
questions.explanation: Aluminum oxide and creep can cause high-resistance heating. Use listed connectors (often CO/ALR or Al-rated) and torque. Do not put unmarked aluminum under a copper-only device.

choices.body: To reduce high-resistance heating from oxidation and conductor creep
Aluminum never needs torque because it is soft
Any copper-only device is acceptable on aluminum
Oil from a refrigeration compressor is the listed antioxidant for all aluminum splices

questions.prompt: A photocell or occupancy sensor that switches the hot should not switch the equipment grounding conductor because:
questions.explanation: The EGC must remain a continuous fault path. Switching a ground can leave equipment unbonded.

choices.body: The equipment grounding path must remain continuous
Grounding conductors are supposed to be switched for three-way control
Photocells only work on neutrals
EGCs carry normal load current and must be switched like hots

questions.prompt: Inrush current of an incandescent or motor load can:
questions.explanation: Briefly exceed running current. Overcurrent devices must be able to handle inrush without nuisance trip while still protecting the conductors.

choices.body: Exceed running current for a short time
Never exceed FLA
Only occur on fiber circuits
Reduce conductor heating below continuous load

questions.prompt: A shared neutral on two ungrounded conductors landed on the same phase will:
questions.explanation: The neutral can carry the sum of both load currents and overheat. Multiwire circuits must be on opposite legs/phases.

choices.body: Carry the sum of the two load currents and can overheat
Carry zero current because the currents cancel on the same phase
Operate as an equipment grounding conductor
Increase the breaker interrupting rating

questions.prompt: A 120-volt load is connected line-to-line on a 240-volt single-phase service by mistake (across two hots). What happens?
questions.explanation: The load sees 240 volts and can be destroyed or become a fire hazard. Verify voltage before connecting.

choices.body: The load is subjected to 240 volts and can be damaged
The load still sees 120 volts because of the neutral
The breaker will always prevent any damage in every case
The equipment grounding conductor will drop the voltage to 120

questions.prompt: A control transformer secondary should be fused (or otherwise protected) because:
questions.explanation: A shorted coil or wiring can overheat the transformer. Protection is sized to the transformer and conductors, not to 'whatever is in the truck.'

choices.body: A secondary short can overheat the transformer and wiring
Fusing the secondary prevents all primary shocks
Control transformers cannot produce hazardous voltage
Secondary protection replaces lockout of the line side

questions.prompt: Electronic loads with high harmonic content can overheat a shared neutral because:
questions.explanation: Triplen harmonics add in the neutral rather than canceling. Neutral current can exceed any phase current. This is why some feeders need an oversized neutral.

choices.body: Triplen harmonics can add in the neutral instead of canceling
Harmonics cancel all neutral current to zero
Harmonics only affect fiber-optic neutrals
A GFCI always blocks harmonics

questions.prompt: A motor circuit includes short-circuit protection and separate overload protection because:
questions.explanation: Short-circuit/ground-fault devices clear high-level faults. Overload devices (heaters, dual-element fuses, or electronic overloads) protect from sustained overload. One device may not do both jobs well.

choices.body: High-level faults and sustained overloads are different duties
Motors never need overload protection if a breaker is present
Overload heaters clear bolted faults faster than any breaker
The equipment grounding conductor provides overload protection

categories.name: Installation & Code Fundamentals
categories.description: Broadly applicable installation and electrical-code principles.

questions.prompt: Conductors in a box must have enough free length so that:
questions.explanation: There must be sufficient free conductor to make up devices without strain. This is a workmanship and code principle, not a manufacturer quirk.

choices.body: Splices and devices can be made up without straining the conductors
The box can be overfilled without limit
Insulation can be stripped back to the clamp as a goal
Grounding conductors can be omitted if the box is plastic

questions.prompt: NM cable passing through wood studs is protected by:
questions.explanation: Steel plates or sufficient setback from the edge so nails do not puncture the cable.

choices.body: Setback from the edge or nail plates as required
Paint only
Duct tape
Leaving the cable on the face of the stud

questions.prompt: A receptacle in a wet location generally needs:
questions.explanation: A weather-resistant device and an enclosure/cover suitable for the location (often extra-duty while in use, depending on the installation). Do not use an indoor device outdoors unsheltered.

choices.body: A device and cover rated for the wet location
An indoor duplex with no cover because rain is grounding
A cardboard cover
No GFCI consideration ever in wet locations

questions.prompt: Equipment must be installed with working space in front so that:
questions.explanation: A worker can operate and service the equipment safely. Blocking a panel with storage is a common violation of that principle.

choices.body: A worker can access and operate the equipment safely
The panel can be used as a shelf
Doors can swing into the worker with no path out
The working space can be used as a storage closet

questions.prompt: Splices must be made in:
questions.explanation: Listed boxes or enclosures with covers, not buried open in plaster or in a wall without access.

choices.body: An accessible box or listed enclosure
Open wall cavities without a box
Underground without a listed method
Inside a fuel-gas furnace heat exchanger

questions.prompt: The grounded (neutral) conductor in typical US AC wiring is identified by:
questions.explanation: White or gray is the standard identification for grounded conductors. Green or bare is equipment grounding.

choices.body: White or gray identification
Green or green with yellow stripe as the preferred neutral
Orange always
Bare copper as the preferred neutral on NM cable

questions.prompt: Equipment grounding conductors are typically identified by:
questions.explanation: Green, green with yellow stripe, or bare.

choices.body: Green, green with yellow, or bare
White only
Gray only
Red only

questions.prompt: Box fill must be calculated because:
questions.explanation: Overfilled boxes overheat, damage insulation, and make devices up unsafely. Count conductors, devices, and fittings as required.

choices.body: Overfilling can damage insulation and create heat and shock hazards
Boxes are allowed unlimited conductors if the cover goes on
Fill only matters for fiber
Device yokes never count

questions.prompt: Torque marks on a breaker lug matter because:
questions.explanation: Under-torque causes heating; over-torque damages the lug or conductor. Use a torque tool to the listing.

choices.body: Correct torque reduces high-resistance heating and damage
Breakers are designed to be tightened until the handle breaks
Torque values are only for automotive work
Aluminum and copper use any random tightness

questions.prompt: A continuous load is often calculated at 125% for overcurrent and conductor sizing because:
questions.explanation: Continuous operation produces more heat. The 125% factor (where applicable) keeps conductors and devices within temperature limits. Exact applications are in the electrical code; the principle is thermal.

choices.body: Heat from long-duration current requires extra capacity
Continuous loads produce no heat
125% reduces voltage to the load
The factor replaces equipment grounding

questions.prompt: SE cable used as a service-entrance method must be:
questions.explanation: Listed, supported, protected from physical damage, and terminated with suitable fittings. Interior routing must follow the rules for the cable type.

choices.body: Listed for the use, supported, and protected from damage
Stripped of its covering and fished like fixture wire as a standard
Run across a sharp roof edge without protection
Used as a flexible jumper on a motor shaft

questions.prompt: A grounding electrode system is intended to:
questions.explanation: Connect the electrical system to earth for lightning, surge, and earth-fault reference. It is not a substitute for the equipment grounding conductor that clears faults.

choices.body: Connect the system to earth; it does not replace the equipment grounding conductor
Carry all normal ungrounded load current
Replace overcurrent devices
Allow omission of EGC to receptacles

questions.prompt: When two grounding electrode types are present (for example rod and metal water pipe), they are typically:
questions.explanation: Bonded together to form one grounding electrode system so they are not at different potentials.

choices.body: Bonded together into one grounding electrode system
Left isolated so they cannot interact
Connected only to isolated equipment grounds, never the service
Used as spare neutrals

questions.prompt: Kitchen small-appliance branch circuits (where used) are intended to:
questions.explanation: Serve receptacle loads in kitchen/dining areas so lighting or other circuits are not overloaded. Exact required numbers are code-edition specific; the principle is dedicated capacity for those loads.

choices.body: Provide capacity for kitchen/dining receptacle loads rather than sharing randomly with lighting only
Replace the service grounding electrode
Feed only hardwired ranges as their sole use in every dwelling
Be wired with speaker cable

questions.prompt: A bathroom receptacle near a basin is commonly GFCI-protected because:
questions.explanation: Water and grounded surfaces increase shock risk. GFCI is a personnel-protection practice in wet areas. Specific locations can vary by code edition; the hazard principle is stable.

choices.body: Water and grounded surfaces increase shock hazard
GFCI increases voltage to hair dryers
Bathroom receptacles cannot be used for portable loads
GFCI replaces the equipment grounding conductor in all bathrooms

questions.prompt: Conduit fill is limited so that:
questions.explanation: Conductors can dissipate heat and be pulled without damaging insulation. Exceeding fill also makes future pulls destructive.

choices.body: Heat can dissipate and conductors can be installed without damage
The conduit can be used as a water pipe
Fill limits only apply to fiber
More conductors always cool each other

questions.prompt: A disconnecting means for a motor or appliance should be located so that:
questions.explanation: A worker can shut off the equipment. Within sight is a common requirement for many motors/appliances; the principle is ready isolation.

It is hidden in a locked remote closet with no identification
It only opens the equipment grounding conductor

Unidentified breakers are safer because nobody will turn them off

Dielectric unions always improve fault clearing
Plumbing changes cannot affect electrical safety

choices.body: The device must be able to safely clear the available fault current
Interrupting rating only needs to exceed the load FLA

questions.explanation: Avoid paralleling neutrals incorrectly. A four-pole switched-neutral transfer (or equivalent design) is used when both sources have bonded neutrals so that objectionable current and multiple bonds do not occur. Follow the system design; do not add a second bond casually at the downstream panel.

Always solid-neutral transfer with two bonded sources as a universal rule
Disconnect the equipment grounding conductor during transfer as a standard

choices.body: GFCI devices that may feed it, and voltage at that receptacle
The utility substation first
The grounding electrode rod length first
The transformer turns ratio first

questions.explanation: Verify voltage at the breaker terminals, then at the first device. A tripped GFCI, open splice, or failed breaker can all present as a dead circuit.

Megger the utility primary as the first residential step

questions.explanation: Mechanical lock, failed start component, or single-phasing. Do not keep resetting a breaker without investigation.

Whether the equipment grounding conductor is too long as the usual cause of humming
Whether the device is unlisted for color
Whether the nameplate is in metric

questions.prompt: A GFCI receptacle will not reset. What is a sound first check?
questions.explanation: A standing ground fault on the load side, line/load reversed, or a failed device. Remove load-side connections and retry before condemning the entire panel.

choices.body: Whether a load-side fault exists or line/load leads are reversed
Whether the water heater anode is spent
Whether the service drop is aluminum
Whether the panel directory uses pencil

questions.explanation: Voltage drop from inrush on a high-impedance supply path. Investigate connections, conductor size, and source capacity—not a smaller breaker.

choices.body: Voltage drop from starting current on a weak or high-resistance supply path
A GFCI that is too sensitive to light
An AFCI that increases voltage

A missing grounding electrode as the usual three-way symptom
A water-logged expansion tank
A failed water-heater T&P valve

choices.body: A short or ground fault on the circuit
A normal inrush that should be ignored
That the breaker is definitely too small for 14 AWG as the only explanation
That the utility voltage is too low as the usual immediate-trip cause

High voltage as the measured 10% low condition
A grounding electrode that is too conductive
A GFCI on a lighting circuit in another building

Whether the grounding rod is copper-coated

Whether NM cable was used on the 5 kV utility line
